entries.hay: taj mahal uttar pradesh northern india heritage an ivory-white marble masterpiece of eternal love and unesco world heritage wonder the taj mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the yamuna river in agra, commissioned by mughal emperor shah jahan in 1631. commissioned in 1631 by the mughal emperor shah jahan to house the tomb of his favourite wife, mumtaz mahal, the taj mahal is recognized worldwide as the jewel of muslim art in india and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage. set within a vast 17-hectare mughal charbagh garden complex with reflecting pools, red sandstone mosques, and intricate marble pietra dura inlay, it stands as an enduring symbol of eternal love. unesco world heritage mughal architecture pietra dura marble inlay charbagh gardens yamuna river views agra fort a monumental 16th-century mughal fortress of red sandstone, featuring jahangiri mahal, diwan-i-am, diwan-i-khas, and breathtaking views of the taj mahal across the yamuna. mehtab bagh the historic charbagh moonlight garden situated perfectly across the yamuna river, renowned as the ultimate sunset vantage point for reflection photos of the taj mahal. tomb of i'timād-ud-daulah (baby taj) often described as a 'jewel box' and the precursor to the taj mahal, this exquisite white marble mausoleum features delicate jali latticework and floral pietra dura inlay. fatehpur sikri the fortified 16th-century mughal capital founded by emperor akbar, home to the colossal buland darwaza, jama masjid, panch mahal, and the serene tomb of salim chishti. akbar's tomb, sikandra an architectural masterpiece combining red sandstone and white marble, set inside a vast 119-acre garden inhabited by peacocks and blackbucks. jama masjid, agra a monumental 17th-century congregational mosque built by jahanara begum, showcasing graceful inverted dome architecture and red sandstone courtyards. chini ka rauza the historic funerary monument of mughal scholar-poet afzal khan shirazi, famous for its rare indo-persian glazed polychrome enamel tiles. taj nature walk a serene 180-acre nature reserve and forested trail located just 500 meters from the east gate of taj mahal, offering elevated viewing towers and rich birdlife. oyo taj mahal view budget stay wifi ac rooftop cafe luggage storage oyo verified budget choice near east gate goa goa konkan coast beach sun, sand and soul golden beaches, portuguese heritage, vibrant nightlife and fresh seafood. goa, india's smallest state, punches well above its weight as a travel destination. with 101km of coastline divided between the busy northern beaches and the quieter south, plus a unesco-listed old city quarter, spice plantations and some of asia's best beach parties, goa is truly an all-seasons destination. beaches nightlife portuguese heritage seafood baga beach north goa's most vibrant beach, renowned for water sports, lively beach shacks, and golden sunsets along the arabian sea. old goa churches unesco world heritage ensemble of portuguese colonial churches, including the basilica of bom jesus and church of st. francis of assisi. palolem beach south goa's tranquil crescent-shaped bay with calm waters, colorful beach huts, sea kayaking, and dolphin-spotting cruises. dudhsagar waterfalls a breathtaking four-tiered waterfall on the mandovi river plunging 310 meters through the lush western ghats forest near the goa-karnataka border. fontainhas latin quarter asia's oldest latin quarter featuring charming portuguese heritage architecture with brightly painted yellow, green, and blue villas, vintage tiled roofs, and art galleries. spice plantation tour immersive guided tour through organic cardamom, cinnamon, pepper, vanilla, and betel nut placeNames: Lord Shiva Temple of Mangalagauri Complex
entries.hay: mangla gauri temple bihar magadh (southern bihar) spiritual maa mangla gauri — the supreme upa-shaktipith of magadh & gaya hill sanctum maa mangla gauri temple on mangalagauri hill in gaya is one of the 18 maha shakti peethas, where the breast of goddess sati fell according to sacred puranic scriptures. dating back to the 15th century and mentioned in the padma purana, vayu purana, and agni purana, the temple features an east-facing hilltop sanctum housing the sacred breast stone (sthana pitha) of goddess shakti. the complex also encompasses ancient shrines of lord shiva, ganesha, and maa kali. one of 18 maha shakti peethas ancient 15th-century hilltop sanctum sacred akhand deep (eternal flame) panoramic overlook of ancient gaya maa mangla gauri main sanctum revered shaktipith sanctum housing the sacred sthana pitha and burning akhand deep. mangalagauri hill stone steps & viewpoint steep flight of stone stairs leading up the hill with panoramic views over the temple roofs of gaya. lord shiva temple of mangalagauri complex ancient stone temple dedicated to lord shiva as bhairava protecting the shaktipith sanctum. brahmayoni sacred hill & rebirth caves sacred peak with 424 stone steps and narrow natural rock passages symbolizing spiritual rebirth. falgu riverbank devghat promenade vibrant riverside ghats where morning snan, vedic chants, and ancestral offerings take place. vishnupad temple complex famous 1787 black basalt temple enshrining lord vishnu’s sacred footprint. gaya surya kund & sun shrine ancient stepped water tank flanked by stone sculptures of the sun god standing on a seven-horse chariot. akshayavat sacred tree enclave immortal banyan tree revered since the ramayana era for the final completion of sacred rites. hotel grand mangla restaurant ac free wifi room service city center comfort

ashokdham temple bihar anga / lakhisarai (eastern bihar) spiritual ashokdham dham — the sacred indradamneshwar mahadev & giant black stone lingam ashokdham temple (indradamneshwar mahadev mandir) in lakhisarai enshrines a colossal ancient black granite shiva lingam discovered by boy ashok in 1977. situated at the confluence of the kiul and harohar rivers in lakhisarai district, ashokdham is celebrated for its colossal black basalt shiva lingam, believed to have been originally worshipped by 8th-century king indradyumna of the pala dynasty. excavated in april 1977, the sacred pilgrimage center features a majestic nagara-style stone temple complex, sacred ponds, and nearby ancient buddhist stupas. colossal black granite indradamneshwar lingam pala-era 8th-century historical heritage shringirishi dham hill sacred springs nongarh & rajauna buddhist excavation stupas indradamneshwar mahadev main sanctum towering stone temple sanctum housing the colossal black granite shiva lingam. shringirishi dham hills & sacred springs scenic hill hermitage associated with sage rishyasringa, featuring freshwater spring kunds. jalappa asthan (hilltop shrine) hilltop sanctuary dedicated to goddess jalappa, offering panoramic vistas of the kiul basin. nongarh ancient buddhist stupa mound massive 5th-century buddhist brick stupa mound excavated on the banks of the kiul river. rajauna archaeological site & sculptures pala-era archaeological mound that yielded exquisite sandstone buddha and ganesha idols. kiul riverfront & bridge viewpoint scenic riverbank providing gentle breezes and sunset reflections along the historic kiul railway bridges. lakhisarai lai sweet heritage market traditional bazaar famous for gi-recognized crispy khoya-lai, ramdana lai, and sweets. surya mandir pokharama historic lakeside sun temple celebrated for festive chhath gatherings and ancient stone carvings. hotel grand ashokdham restaurant ac free wifi room service city center comfort

placeNames: Bodh Gaya Green Buffer Eco Trail
entries.hay: gautam budha wildlife sanctuary bihar magadh / gaya (southern bihar) wildlife gautam budha sanctuary — dense dry deciduous forests & hill wilderness of magadh gautam budha wildlife sanctuary spans 259 square kilometers across gaya (bihar) and koderma (jharkhand), preserving rich dry deciduous wildlife corridors. named in honor of lord gautama buddha, this expansive sanctuary along the lower chota nagpur and magadh plateau protects thriving populations of leopards, chital deer, sambar, wild boars, indian gazelles (chinkara), and over 150 species of birds. 259-sq-km protected wildlife sanctuary vindhyan & chota nagpur hill ecosystem gurpa hill (kukkutapadagiri buddhist hermitage) chital, sambar, leopard & bird habitat gautam buddha sanctuary core forest dense mixed sal and bamboo forest sheltering leopards, chital, sambar deer, and peacocks. gurpa hill (kukkutapadagiri sacred peak) sacred mountain where mahakashyapa, foremost disciple of buddha, entered supreme meditation. dhobi forest watchtower & waterhole forest observation deck overlooking natural watering holes frequented by deer and wild boars. falgu river upper catchment & rapids picturesque rocky riverbed and natural stream cascades feeding the sacred falgu basin. koderma border ridge & hill trail rugged hill plateau offering panoramic views across the forested boundary of bihar and jharkhand. bodh gaya green buffer eco trail protected forest green belt connecting the wildlife corridor with bodh gaya’s monastic zone. mahuadanr butterfly & birding meadow wildflower meadow hosting dozens of native butterfly species and migratory winter warblers. barabar foothills forest trail forested granite outcrops and trail leading towards ancient 3rd-century bce mauryan rock-cut caves. hotel grand gautam restaurant ac free wifi room service city center comfort

udaypur wildlife sanctuary bihar tirhut / west champaran (northwestern bihar) wildlife udaypur wildlife sanctuary — oxbow lake wetlands & gandak floodplain wilderness udaypur wildlife sanctuary in west champaran spans 8.74 square kilometers of pristine oxbow lake wetlands and swamp forests along the gandak river basin. located near bettiah in west champaran, udaypur sanctuary is formed around a large oxbow lake created by the gandak river. the wetland habitat provides vital breeding grounds for resident waterfowl and migratory birds, including spotted bills, whistling teals, kingfishers, and swamp deer. gandak river oxbow lake wetland valmiki tiger reserve ecological buffer diverse waterfowl & aquatic habitat bettiah raj historic heritage proximity udaypur oxbow lake & bird wetland scenic oxbow lake surrounded by reed beds, sheltering whistling ducks, coots, and jacanas. saraiya man lake (freshwater sanctuary) large picturesque natural lake famous for sweet jamun-filtered waters and migratory bird flocks. bettiah raj palace & historic deorhi grand 18th-century palace complex of the bettiah raj estate featuring colonial courtyards. gandak riverfront & boat safari ghat expansive riverbanks offering country boat safaris to observe river dolphins and waterbirds. lauriya nandangarh ashokan lion pillar pristine 35-foot polished single-stone ashokan pillar crowned by a magnificent lion capital. valmiki tiger reserve forest buffer lush himalayan terai forest harboring bengal tigers, indian rhinos, leopards, and elephants. bhitiharwa gandhi ashram historic ashram founded by mahatma gandhi during the historic champaran satyagraha of 1917. someshwar fort & himalayan foothills highest point in bihar (880m) offering breathtaking views of snowy himalayan peaks and nepal. hotel grand udaypur restaurant ac free wifi room service city center comfort

placeNames: Bhojpur Regional Folk Art & Craft Enclave
entries.hay: aranya devi temple, arrah bihar bhojpur / arrah (western bihar) spiritual maa aranya devi — the forest goddess of mahabharata & historic veer kunwar singh heritage maa aranya devi temple in arrah is an ancient shakti temple dating back to the mahabharata era, enshrining twin stone deities who blessed the pandavas during their exile. located in the historic town of arrah (bhojpur district), aranya devi temple is the presiding patron deity of the city. legend holds that the town was named arrah after maa aranya devi (goddess of the forests), worshipped by king yudhishthira and the pandavas. the district is also world-renowned for babu veer kunwar singh, the legendary 80-year-old hero of india’s 1857 first war of independence, whose historic fort at jagdishpur stands nearby. twin ancient stone deities of maa aranya devi mahabharata-era forest goddess sanctorum historic jagdishpur fort of veer kunwar singh 1857 arrah house historic siege monument maa aranya devi main sanctum ancient stone temple housing the twin rounded stone murtis of aranya devi and sister aditi. veer kunwar singh fort & memorial (jagdishpur) historic fort and ancestral palace of 1857 revolutionary leader babu veer kunwar singh. historic arrah house & 1857 siege monument two-storey colonial billiard room that withstood an eight-day siege by kunwar singh’s forces in 1857. maharaja college heritage hall & museum colonial-era educational heritage campus featuring historic stone arches and regional archives. karisath sun temple (surya mandir) lakeside sun temple featuring ancient stone reliefs of lord surya and vibrant chhath ghats. gangi riverfront & historic bathing ghats tranquil riverfront tributary offering open skies, morning bathing pavilions, and village views. koilwar bridge (historic abdul bari bridge) monumental 1.4-kilometer lattice girder rail-road bridge opened in 1862 across the sacred son river. bhojpur regional folk art & craft enclave artisan quarter kaimur hills in sasaram, maa tara chandi is an ancient tantric shaktipith where goddess sati’s right eye (netra) fell. adjacent to the shrine is an ancient minor rock edict of emperor ashoka (256 bce) entries.hay: kaimur wildlife sanctuary bihar kaimur & rohtas plateau (southwestern bihar) wildlife kaimur sanctuary — bihar’s largest wildlife reserve & proposed 2nd tiger reserve kaimur wildlife sanctuary covers 1,342 square kilometers across kaimur and rohtas districts, featuring rugged vindhyan valleys, prehistoric rock art, and thriving tiger-corridor wildlife. as bihar’s largest protected forest, kaimur wildlife sanctuary spans dense dry deciduous sal forests, dramatic sandstone canyons, and perennial waterfalls like telhar kund and karkat. it serves as a vital corridor for leopards, sloth bears, striped hyenas, chital, blackbucks, and proposed reintroduction of bengal tigers. bihar’s largest wildlife sanctuary (1,342 sq km) proposed bihar 2nd tiger reserve corridor prehistoric cave rock paintings (palaeolithic) telhar kund, karkat & tutla bhawani waterfalls kaimur sanctuary core forest & safari trail sprawling sal forest hosting sloth bears, leopards, nilgai, chital deer, and wild boars. telhar kund waterfall & forest canyon 80-meter sheer plunge waterfall dropping into an emerald canyon surrounded by dense woods. karkat waterfall & river canyon wide picturesque waterfall on the karmanasa river offering boating and birdwatching. adhaura plateau forest vistas cool elevated plateau at 2,000 feet adorned with tribal hamlets, sal groves, and deep valleys. maa mundeshwari hill sanctuary india’s oldest functional stone temple (635 ce) perched on the solitary pavra hill. durgavati reservoir & dam viewpoint vast scenic water reservoir flanked by the forested kaimur foothills. prehistoric rock art caves of kaimur ancient rock shelters displaying upper palaeolithic and mesolithic red-ochre animal drawings. tutla bhawani waterfall & canyon bridge deep forest canyon with 200m suspension bridge leading to the sacred waterfall shrine. hotel grand kaimur restaurant ac free wifi room service city center comfort

entries.hay: munger fort bihar munger / anga (eastern bihar) heritage munger fort — the ancient ganga citadel & world capital of modern yoga munger fort is a legendary stone fortress built on a rocky promontory overlooking the holy river ganga, dating back to the karna of mahabharata and bengal nawab mir qasim. rising grandly on the southern banks of the river ganga, munger fort spans 222 acres enclosed by massive stone ramparts and a wide moat. historically held by the guptas, palas, karnas, and nawab mir qasim who shifted bengal’s capital here in 1762, the fort today houses the globally renowned bihar school of yoga (ganga darshan), the sacred chandika sthan shaktipith, and thermal sita kund springs. historic 222-acre riverfront stone citadel bihar school of yoga (ganga darshan ashram) chandika sthan shaktipith (sati’s left eye) sita kund & rishikund geothermal springs munger fort ramparts & lal darwaza massive stone ramparts, historic brick battlements, and the grand lal darwaza gateway overlooking the ganga. bihar school of yoga (ganga darshan) world-renowned yoga ashram founded in 1964 by swami satyananda saraswati overlooking the ganga. chandika sthan shaktipith revered shaktipith where goddess sati’s left eye fell, known for granting wishes to eye ailments. kastaharni ghat (sacred ganga snan ghat) sacred riverfront ghat where the ganga flows northwards buxar fort bihar bhojpur / buxar (western bihar) heritage buxar fort — the ganga river citadel & battle of buxar historic grounds buxar fort stands on a high bluff overlooking the sacred river ganga in buxar, famous for vedic hermitage lore of sage vishwamitra and the historic 1764 battle of buxar. erected in 1054 ce by king rudra deo of the paramara dynasty and fortified through the mughal and british eras, buxar fort commands spectacular views over the sacred ganga. the historic town is legendary as the tapovan of sage vishwamitra where lord rama slew demoness tadaka, as well as the site of the pivotal 1764 battle of buxar and the 1539 battle of chausa. 11th-century ganga riverfront stone fortress battle of buxar (1764) monument at katkauli ramrekha ghat (lord rama’s holy bathing ghat) chausa battlefield & memorial (1539 ce) buxar fort citadel & ganga viewpoint medieval stone fort bastion perched on the ganga bluff with ancient carved subterranean cells. ramrekha ghat (sacred ganga promenade) holy riverfront bathing ghat where lord rama and lakshmana crossed the ganga with sage vishwamitra. katkauli maidan (battle of buxar 1764 monument) historic battleground and british victory stone obelisk commemorating the historic october 1764 battle. chausa battlefield & historic monument famous riverfront site where sher shah suri defeated mughal emperor humayun in june 1539. vishwamitra ashram (charitravan) ancient hermitage complex where sage vishwamitra taught divine astras to lord rama. ahirauli devi ahilya temple & kund sacred village temple commemorating the redemption of devi ahilya from a stone curse by rama’s lotus touch. brahmapur baba bameshwar nath temple ancient westward-facing swayambhu shiva temple renowned for massive cattle and pilgrim fairs during shivratri. naulakha mandir (charitravan buxar) intricately sculpted marble south indian-style temple complex constructed in the early 20th century. hotel grand buxar restaurant ac free wifi entries.hay: darbhanga fort bihar mithila / darbhanga (northern bihar) heritage darbhanga fort — the royal red-brick citadel of raj darbhanga & mithila cultural capital darbhanga fort (rambagh palace walls) in darbhanga is a massive 1934 red-brick royal citadel built by maharaja kameshwar singh of the khandavala dynasty of raj darbhanga. modeled after the red fort in delhi, the fort features a 1-kilometer-long, 90-foot-high monumental red-brick perimeter wall and grand gateways. the royal enclave encompasses the rambagh palace, the italianate anand bagh palace, nargona palace (india’s first earthquake-resistant royal residence), the revered shyama mai kali temple, and world-class museums housing priceless gold thrones and mithila manuscripts. massive 1-km red-brick royal citadel wall maharaja rameshwar singh, revered for divine grace. anand bagh palace & kameshwar singh museum opulent european-style palace housing the maharajadhiraja kameshwar singh kalyani foundation museum. nargona palace (first earthquake-resistant palace) innovative palace constructed in 1939 with earthquake-resistant engineering, now housing lnmu. chandradhari museum of mithila antiquities celebrated manokamna temple (carved red stone shrine) beautifully sculpted modern red-sandstone temple dedicated to lord hanuman, situated inside royal gardens. hotel grand darbhanga restaurant ac free wifi room service city center comfort

entries.hay: gurdwara bal lila maini sangat bihar patna (central bihar) heritage gurdwara bal lila — the childhood play palace of guru gobind singh ji & sacred chulha sahib gurdwara bal lila maini sangat in patna city marks the historic palace of raja fateh chand maini, where child gobind rai spent his early childhood playing and blessing rani maini. situated just a few hundred paces from takht sri patna sahib, gurdwara bal lila is a deeply revered sikh historical sanctuary. child gobind rai (later guru gobind singh ji) would sit in the lap of childless rani maini, who lovingly served him boiled gram (chhola-poori). to this day, the unique prasad of boiled spiced chickpeas is served to all visitors from the historic chulha sahib hearth. childhood palace of guru gobind singh ji historic chulha sahib sacred hearth traditional chhola-poori prasad custom takht sri patna sahib heritage corridor gurdwara bal lila main sanctum & darbar white marble darbar hall preserving the sacred cradle and holy guru granth sahib. historic chulha sahib (rani maini hearth) sacred hearth where boiled spiced grams are prepared continuously and served as unique prasad. takht sri harmandir ji patna sahib one of the five holy takhts of sikhism marking the birthplace of guru gobind singh ji. gurdwara guru ka bagh historic garden site where guru tegh bahadur ji rested on his return from assam. gurdwara gai ghat (bhai jetha ji shrine) sacred riverfront shrine where guru nanak dev ji stayed on his first udasi. mangal talab & historic city promenades historic excavated water tank and public park serving as a peaceful communal retreat in old patna. paduka sahib sacred footprint shrine sacred shrine preserving the holy wooden footwear (khadau) of guru tegh bahadur ji. sabhyata dwar & ganga riverfront promenade monumental 32-meter mauryan archway on the scenic riverfront promenade along the ganga. hotel grand gurdwara restaurant ac free wifi room service city center comfort

enshrining the footprint of lord rama and konhara ghat, the mythical site of gajendra moksha. subterranean (patala) shiva lingam sanctum ramchaura mandir (footprint of lord rama) konhara ghat entries.hay: vikramshila gangetic dolphin sanctuary bihar anga / bhagalpur (eastern bihar) wildlife vikramshila dolphin sanctuary — river dolphins of the holy ganga & ancient vikramshila university vikramshila gangetic dolphin sanctuary spans 65 kilometers of the river ganga from sultanganj to kahalgaon in bhagalpur, the only designated protected sanctuary for endangered gangetic dolphins in asia. protecting the national aquatic animal of india (platanista gangetica), this river sanctuary shelters over 300 freshwater gangetic dolphins (susu), smooth-coated otters, gharials, and endangered indian skimmers. the region is rich in heritage, including the 8th-century vikramshila ancient buddhist university, the rock-island temple of ajgaibinath at sultanganj, and the bateshwar sthan cliff placeNames: Cyclopean Wall of Rajgir (40-km Stone Rampart)
entries.hay: pant wildlife sanctuary bihar magadh / rajgir (southern bihar) wildlife pant wildlife sanctuary — the five sacred hills of rajgir & historic peace pagoda pant wildlife sanctuary in rajgir covers 35.8 square kilometers across the historic five hills (vipulagiri, ratnagiri, gridhrakuta, udaygiri, and sona giri), rich in ancient buddhist and jain lore. cradled in a green valley encircled chakrata uttarakhand garhwal hill_station chakrata — untouched deodar haven of uttarakhand chakrata is a secluded cantonment town in uttarakhand, famous for majestic deodar forests, tiger falls, and panoramic himalayan vistas. perched at an elevation of 2,118 meters in the garhwal himalayas of uttarakhand, chakrata is an idyllic retreat enveloped in whispering deodar, pine, and oak woodlands. founded as a british indian army cantonment in 1869, the town retains its peaceful, unhurried colonial charm free from commercial crowds. from the roaring 312-foot plunge of tiger falls to the 300-km himalayan panoramas from deoban and golden hour sunsets at chilmiri neck, chakrata offers an authentic mountain sanctuary for nature enthusiasts, trekkers, and peace seekers. deodar forests waterfalls himalayan views alpine treks quiet cantonment tiger falls one of the highest direct waterfalls in uttarakhand, plummeting 312 feet (95 meters) into a crystal-clear natural plunge pool surrounded by dense oak and deodar canopy. deoban (devban) situated at an altitude of 2,865 meters amidst ancient deodar forests, deoban offers sweeping 300-km panoramic vistas of the greater himalayas, including chaukhamba and nanda devi peaks. chilmiri neck the highest peak in chakrata cantonment, famed for mesmerizing 360-degree sunset panoramas, rolling mountain ridges, and views of the yamuna valley and rohru hills. budher caves & moila danda an emerald undulating alpine bugyal (meadow) trek leading to the fascinating miola tibba and unexplored ancient limestone stalactite caves and historic pari tibba temple. kanasar deodar forest home to asia’s oldest and largest deodar cedar trees with trunk circumferences exceeding 6 meters, surrounded by rolling lush meadows and historic wooden forest rest houses. ram tal horticultural garden peaceful terraced mountain garden featuring a natural alpine pond, diverse birdlife, blossoming apple and plum orchards, and tranquil green picnic lawns.
